name: Acrobatics
description: The character has learned the art of acrobatic maneuvering, having spent time with a theater company, in one of the fencing schools of Yndaros or climbing the trees of Davokar. The nimbleness of the acrobat provides an advantage when trying to withdraw from close combat or when quickly wanting to reach the center of an enemy formation.
novice: [Rea] Test [Qui] to avoid Free Attacks when moving/withdrawing from melee. Fail: Stay put or move & suffer Free Attack.
adept: [Free] If knocked down, test [Qui] to stand up as Free Action. Fail: Spend Move Action to stand.
master: [Rea] Once/turn, use enemy as shield. Target takes hit instead of character (no Defense allowed). Requires successful [Qui] test.

name: Alchemy
description: The character is schooled in the mysteries of alchemy. With the right ingredients, the character can prepare various elixirs to help it survive in the dark depths of Davokar...
novice: [Spec] Test [Cun] to create 1 dose of Novice elixir.
adept: [Spec] Test [Cun] to create 1 dose of Adept elixir OR 1D4 doses of Novice elixir.
master: [Spec] Test [Cun] to create 1 dose of Master elixir, 1D4 Adept doses, OR 1D8 Novice doses.

name: Backstab
description: The palace of Yndaros, the alleys of Thistle Hold and the gloom of Davokar are extremely different surroundings, but they have at least one thing in common: when arguments fail, the blades speak up...
novice: [Rea] Once/turn, one attack with Advantage deals +1D4 dmg. Can use [Dis] instead of [Acc] on Advantage attacks.
adept: [Rea] As Novice, plus bleeding wound: enemy takes 1D4 dmg/turn until healed.
master: [Rea] As Adept, but deals +1D8 dmg. No limit on backstabs/turn. All Advantage attacks count as backstabs.

name: Berserker
description: The feared barbarian warriors of Davokar have developed the practice of working themselves into a berserker frenzy before battle...
novice: [Free] Enter frenzy: Deal +1D6 melee dmg, but Defense attribute counts as 5.
adept: [Rea] While frenzied, ignore 1D4 dmg from each hit.
master: [Free] Frenzy deals +1D6 dmg and ignores 1D4 incoming dmg, but Defense is calculated normally.

name: Dominate
description: With nothing but presence, gaze and voice, strong personalities can force weaker minds to bend in the midst of a raging battle...
novice: [Pas] Use [Per] instead of [Acc] in melee.
adept: [Free] Test [Per←Res] to make enemy hesitate (no attack this turn, attacks ally if possible).
master: [Act] Test [Per←Res] to subdue enemy (negotiate/flee/surrender). In combat, target must be wounded first.

name: Iron fist
description: The character is trained to use its strength for maximum effect on a target in melee combat. Knights, members of the barbarian Wrathguard and other heavily armed warriors rely on their strength in combat...
novice: [Pas] Use [Str] instead of [Acc] for melee attacks.
adept: [Pas] Melee attacks deal +1D4 dmg.
master: [Act] Once/turn, perform heavy attack dealing +1D8 dmg (replaces Adept +1D4).

name: Loremaster
description: The character is educated and well-versed in the ways of the world: its cultures, its history, languages and artifacts...
novice: [Free] Test [Cun] to identify artifacts or translate human languages. Simple phrases need no test.
adept: [Free] Use [Cun] to activate artifacts. Test [Cun] to read/speak Elvish or Troll.
master: [Free] Test [Cun] to activate scrolls. Use [Cun] vs [Res] to resist mystical effects. Test [Cun] to read Symbaroum language.

name: Man-at-arms
description: A real warrior wears armor and is trained in how to move and fight while doing so. This is true among Ambrians and barbarians alike...
novice: [Pas] Increase Armor tier by one step (Light 1D6, Medium 1D8, Heavy 1D10).
adept: [Pas] Armor no longer penalizes [Qui] or abilities based on [Qui] (inc. Defense). Impeding still affects magic.
master: [Rea] Test [Qui] to negate Armor-piercing/reducing effects (except mystical powers).

name: Anathema
description: The mystic has studied the secrets of countering magic and can dispel the effects of other powers. Anathema does not affect rituals...
novice: [Act] Test [Res←Res] to dispel ongoing power on self or creature.
adept: [Act] Dispel multiple targets in a Chain (test for each).
master: [Act] Test [Res] to dispel all mystical effects, summoned creatures, etc.

name: Brimstone cascade
description: The mystic can unleash the rampaging spirit of fire and burn its enemies to cinders, or at least scorch them severely.
novice: [Act] Test [Res←Qui]. Success: 1D12 dmg. Fail: 1D6 dmg.
adept: [Act] As Novice, but creates Chain. If target takes full 1D12 dmg, arc to next target until test fails.
master: [Act] As Adept, but Chain continues even on failed test (dealing 1D6). Stops after second failure.

name: Lay on hands
description: The secrets of life lay bare for the mystic and with them follows the coveted power of healing, often interpreted as a gift from whichever deity the mystic adheres to.
novice: [Act] Touch & Test [Res] to heal 1D6 [Tgh]. Works on self.
adept: [Act] Heals 1D8 [Tgh] and cures poison/bleeding.
master: [Act] Ranged healing (sight). Heals 1D8 [Tgh] + cures poison/bleeding. Touch healing increases to 1D12 [Tgh].

name: Maltransformation
description: The mystic has grasped that physical appearance is a dynamic concept, and knows how to use that insight to transform its enemies into weaker forms.
novice: [Act] Test [Res]. Turn target into harmless beast. Sustained by [Res←Res] each turn. Target keeps Attributes but loses abilities/items.
adept: [Act] Ongoing effect. No concentration needed. Ends on failed [Res←Res] test.
master: [Act] Creates Chain of transformations. Ongoing until [Res] test fails (check per target/turn).

name: Blood Bond
description: The corrupting effect of magic is of course well known to mystics. Sometimes the Corruption is a necessary price to pay...
novice: Share Corruption with familiar. Test [Res]. Success: -1D4 Perm. Corr for mystic, +1D6 Perm. Corr for familiar. Costs 1 XP. If familiar turns abomination, it attacks.

name: Familiar
description: The mystic binds itself to a beast. This beast is not much smarter than others of its kind, but is fiercely loyal...
novice: Bind a beast companion. Telepathic link & shared senses. Can transfer 50% damage between mystic/familiar. If familiar dies, mystic takes 1D8 dmg (ign. Armor). Gains XP.

name: Bushcraft
description: The character can survive on meager resources and is used to finding food and shelter in harsh terrain...
novice: Test [Vig] to find food/water for self in wild/ruins. Group (max 5) requires time. Gather 1D6 rations/day (move) or 1D10 (stay). Can take multiple times for harsher terrains.

name: Robust
description: The character belongs to a race of creatures that are naturally tall and often continue to grow their entire lives. But there are variations...
novice: [Spec] Ignore 1D4 dmg/hit. Deal +1D4 melee dmg once/turn. Def based on [Qui-2]. Light armor only (cost x2).
adept: [Spec] Ignore 1D6 dmg/hit. Deal +1D6 melee dmg once/turn. Def based on [Qui-3]. Light armor only (cost x3).
master: [Spec] Ignore 1D8 dmg/hit. Deal +1D8 melee dmg once/turn. Def based on [Qui-4]. Light armor only (cost x4).

name: Undead
description: The creature is a spirit trapped inside a dead body. The spirit controls the slowly decaying corpse and is banished when the body is destroyed.
novice: I [Pas] Immune to poison/disease. No Pain Threshold. No natural/alchemical healing. Eat meat/drink blood to heal (1 consumed = 2 [Tgh]).
adept: II [Pas] Half dmg from physical effects/elements. Full dmg from magic ignoring armor.
master: III [Pas] Half dmg from alchemy/mystical effects. Full dmg from magical weapons/holy effects.

name: Acrobatics
description: The character has learned the art of acrobatic maneuvering, having spent time with a theater company, in one of the fencing schools of Yndaros or climbing the trees of Davokar. The nimbleness of the acrobat provides an advantage when trying to withdraw from close combat or when quickly wanting to reach the center of an enemy formation.
novice: [Rea] Test [Qui] to avoid Free Attacks when moving/withdrawing from melee. Fail: Stay put or move & suffer Free Attack.
adept: [Free] If knocked down, test [Qui] to stand up as Free Action. Fail: Spend Move Action to stand.
master: [Rea] Once/turn, use enemy as shield. Target takes hit instead of character (no Def). Requires successful [Qui] test.

name: Alchemy
description: The character is schooled in the mysteries of alchemy. With the right ingredients, the character can prepare various elixirs to help it survive in the dark depths of Davokar. A list of alchemical mixtures and potions are featured in Chapter 16: Equipment (page 153). In problem-solving situations, Alchemy can be used to identify drugs and poisons and to gain clues as to where they come from. Other than that, the character may attempt to prepare an elixir once per adventure. This attempt can be performed before the start of an adventure or at any appropriate moment during the adventure – for example when traveling through a forest or when passing through a cave where potent ingredients may be found. The alchemists' field of knowledge is constantly growing as old recipes are recovered and new formulas created. With the Advanced Player's Guide alchemists may create more elixirs, all of them listed in the margin on page 62, sorted into separate levels like in the Core Rulebook. The effects of the elixirs are described in the chapter Equipment on page 120. Alchemists are used to working with explosive and volatile substances, and are therefore able to handle alchemical grenades correctly and efficiently. Hence, alchemists – starting at the novice level – do not risk failing catastrophically with alchemical grenades.
novice: [Spec] Test [Cun] to create 1 dose of Novice elixir.
adept: [Spec] Test [Cun] to create 1 dose of Adept elixir OR 1D4 doses of Novice elixir.
master: [Spec] Test [Cun] to create 1 dose of Master elixir, 1D4 Adept doses, OR 1D8 Novice doses.

name: Backstab
description: The palace of Yndaros, the alleys of Thistle Hold and the gloom of Davokar are extremely different surroundings, but they have at least one thing in common: when arguments fail, the blades speak up. The character has learned how to exploit weaknesses in an enemy's defense, and will not let an opportunity go by without making a Backstab.
novice: [Rea] One attack/turn from Advantage deals +1D4 dmg. Can use [Dis] instead of [Acc] on Advantage attacks.
adept: [Rea] As Novice + bleeding wound (1D4 dmg/turn until healed).
master: [Rea] As Adept, but deals +1D8 dmg. No limit on backstabs/turn. All Advantage attacks count as backstabs.

name: Beast lore
description: The character is schooled in the lore of beasts and knows the secrets of most monsters. Many monsters possess special abilities and unique attacks as well as weaknesses which are good to know about when trying to bring them down. At higher levels the character must pick a specialization – Abominations, Beasts, Cultural Beings or Undead – and receives further advantages against members of that specific category. A character with Beast Lore can identify the tracks of many monsters and beings, and use that information to draw conclusions regarding the size and general behavior of the creature – is it hunting, on the run or just passing through?
novice: [Free] Test [Cun] to know monster strengths/weaknesses.
adept: [Free] Pick sub-category. Deal +1D4 dmg to that category. Allies get bonus if instructed.
master: [Free] Deal +1D6 dmg to chosen category. Allies get bonus if instructed.

name: Berserker
description: The feared barbarian warriors of Davokar have developed the practice of working themselves into a berserker frenzy before battle. By letting the repressed anger of the heart strengthen its limbs, the character can unleash a fuming rage that, if channeled correctly, might determine which side will emerge victorious from the battle.
novice: [Free] Enter frenzy: Deal +1D6 melee dmg, but Defense attribute counts as 5.
adept: [Rea] While frenzied, ignore 1D4 dmg from each hit.
master: [Free] Frenzy deals +1D6 dmg & ignores 1D4 incoming dmg, but Defense is calculated normally.

name: Bodyguard
description: High-born Ambrians, rich merchant lords and other potentates surround themselves with bodyguards. Even among the barbarians there are housecarls who serve to protect the life of their chieftain. The character is trained to place itself in the way of painful strikes and lethal blows aimed at the protected person.
novice: [Rea] Test [Res] to take hit for ally. Auto-hit (no Def).
adept: [Rea] As Novice, but can Defend against attack.
master: [Rea] As Adept, plus Free Attack against attacker.

name: Dominate
description: With nothing but presence, gaze and voice, strong personalities can force weaker minds to bend in the midst of a raging battle. The character is trained in this art of subduing combat. Among the gladiators of Yndaros, this is considered to be a particularly impressive way to win a battle, and it is even regarded as extremely honorable among the barbarian clans to overcome your enemy in such a manner. In social situations, this ability can also be used to scare someone into obedience and force secrets out of them.
novice: [Pas] Use [Per] instead of [Acc] in melee.
adept: [Free] Test [Per←Res]. Success: Enemy hesitates (no attack this turn, attacks ally if possible).
master: [Act] Test [Per←Res] to subdue enemy (negotiate/flee/surrender). In combat, target must be wounded first.

name: Equestrian
description: Heavy cavalry dominates the plains of Ambria, a truth proven time and again by Queen Korinthia when she sent her armored horsemen against stubborn barbarians during the first decade of her invasion. It takes training to be able to use a mount in combat, both for the rider and the mount, but if they are able to work together as one, they become a deadly combination. This ability is also efficiently used by the barbarians of the western plains, who launch raids against the settlements of western Ambria using their horse-drawn chariots. A character with the Equestrian ability also has a good hand with other kinds of farm animals and the like, and can therefore use the ability to calm agitated beasts, for instance keeping watch dogs from barking.
novice: [Rea] Deal +1D6 dmg on one melee attack if mount moved first.
adept: [Act] Sweeping attack: Move part before and after attack. Enemy can only React or Chase.
master: [Rea] Charge deals +1D10 dmg (instead of 1D6) if mount moved.

name: Exceptional attribute
description: All the character's senses, as well as its physical and mental capacity, can be improved. By practicing a little bit each day, the muscles can grow stronger, the eyes sharper and intellect vaster. This ability enhances the character's basic survival capability. This ability may be chosen multiple times, each time related to a different Attribute.
novice: [Spec] Attribute +1.
adept: [Spec] Attribute +2 total.
master: [Spec] Attribute +3 total.

name: Feint
description: Persons and creatures that lack the will or strength to wield heavy melee weapons have instead developed techniques for feinting. This ability demands a weapon with either the Short or the Precise quality. Thanks to the skill of the character, these weapons can be handled in a both discreet and confusing manner.
novice: [Pas] Use [Dis] instead of [Acc] with Short/Precise weapon. Counts as Advantage.
adept: [Rea] Use [Dis] instead of [Qui] for Defense.
master: [Act] Test [Dis←Vig] for Free Attack (plus normal attack).

name: Iron fist
description: The character is trained to use its strength for maximum effect on a target in melee combat. Knights, members of the barbarian Wrathguard and other heavily armed warriors rely on their strength in combat and leave precision and finesse for others to worry about.
novice: [Pas] Use [Str] instead of [Acc] in melee.
adept: [Pas] Melee deals +1D4 dmg.
master: [Act] Once/turn, melee attack deals +1D8 dmg (instead of +1D4).

name: Leader
description: There are many who fight their way to a position of leadership, but there are few who get pointed out as true leaders by the people they are meant to lead. If equipped with this ability the character is an inspiring, charismatic and eloquent person whom others listen to and follow, sometimes to their death. Outside of combat, the Leader ability can be useful to seize command over a group of strangers, organize a militia and the like.
novice: [Pas] Use [Per] instead of [Res] (except Corruption Threshold).
adept: [Act] Target enemy/object. Allies deal +1D4 dmg to target for Scene.
master: [Act] Allies use Leader's [Per] instead of their [Res] for Scene.

name: Loremaster
description: The character is educated and well-versed in the ways of the world: its cultures, its history, languages and artifacts. For centuries heroes, monsters and kingdoms have come and gone and left behind powerful items and secret texts. This ability represents knowledge about such objects. Through extensive studies a character with this ability knows not only the story of an object but also its properties and applications. The Loremaster ability also makes the character skilled at researching records and administrative documents, something which might be very useful when faced with those kinds of problems and puzzles.
novice: [Free] Test [Cun] to know artifact properties or translate. Simple phrases need no test.
adept: [Free] Activate artifact powers with [Cun]. Read Elf/Troll tongues ([Cun] for convo).
master: [Free] Activate scrolls with [Cun]. Resist magic with [Cun]. Read Symbaroum tongue.

name: Marksman
description: Marksmen have their natural position in every army, scouting party and band of brigands. The character can inflict serious damage on its enemies with a bow or crossbow, hoping to either bring them down or at least make sure that they do not reach those of the character's allies that are equipped for melee combat.
novice: [Pas] Bow dmg 1D10, Crossbow 1D12.
adept: [Act] If target wounded, test [Acc←Str] when they move. Success: Movement forfeit.
master: [Act] Projectiles ign. Armor.

name: Man-at-arms
description: A real warrior wears armor and is trained in how to move and fight while doing so. This is true among Ambrians and barbarians alike, even if the most heavily armored warriors usually are of Ambrian stock. No matter what the armor is made from, be it leather, steel or any other material, the Man-at-arms ability gives the character increased protection against hostile strikes and blows.
novice: [Pas] Armor tier +1 step (Light 1D6, Med 1D8, Heavy 1D10).
adept: [Pas] Armor doesn't penalize [Qui] (Def/Abilities). Impeding still affects magic.
master: [Rea] Test [Qui] to keep Armor vs armor-piercing/reducing effects (not magic).

name: Medicus
description: The character is schooled in the art of healing and therefore a greatly coveted asset in its society, whether he or she keeps diseases from spreading, takes care of wounded warriors or tends to the ruling elite. The art of healing has been developed in parallel with alchemy, and many healers are also trained in alchemy for this reason, especially those who operate far from civilization where there are no herbal cures to buy from well-stocked merchants. A character with the Medicus ability can diagnose and cure diseases and identify a poison by its symptoms. Medicus also gives the character a coroner's point of view, which might come in handy when examining a crime scene or a dead body.
novice: [Act] Test [Cun] to heal 1D4 (1D6 w/ kit). Once/patient/day.
adept: [Act] Heal 1D6 (1D8 w/ kit).
master: [Act] Heal 1D8 (1D10 w/ kit). Fail heals 1D4 (1D6 w/ kit).

name: Mystical power
description: The character has access to one or more mystical powers. These powers have either been obtained as a gift, a curse, through assiduous studies or as a consequence of a deep and dedicated faith. The character's power may belong to a mystical tradition (Wizardry, Sorcery, Theurgy or Witchcraft), which all have their benefits and disadvantages. The character may also be a Mystic without a tradition, with a homebrewed theory as to where these powers come from and what they are meant for. For more information see Chapter 18: Mystical Traditions (page 126). Each Mystical Power is its own ability and is purchased separately. For a more detailed description of the different mystical powers, see Chapter 19: Mystical Powers (page 130). The character suffers one point (1) of permanent Corruption each time he or she learns a new mystical power. The Corruption can be reduced if the power is part of a mystical tradition that the character belongs to. The character also suffers 1d4 temporary Corruption each time this power is used. Again, the Corruption suffered can be reduced if the power is considered a part of a tradition that the character belongs to (see Shadow & Corruption, page 174).
novice: [Spec] Master Novice power. +1 Perm. Corr. 1D4 Temp. Corr/use.
adept: [Spec] Master Adept power.
master: [Spec] Master Master power.

name: Natural warrior
description: A sword or a bow is not always needed to fight. Through long and hard training, the character has become a dangerous opponent even when unarmed. The barbarians of the forests have proud traditions of wrestling and boxing. Another example is the fighting style developed in the gutters of eastern Yndaros, a style that nowadays can be seen at the Dome since a pair of the city's renowned gladiators have embraced its techniques.
novice: [Pas] Unarmed deals 1D6 dmg. Stacks with Natural Weapons trait.
adept: [Act] Perform double attack against single target.
master: [Pas] Unarmed deals +1D6 extra dmg per hit.

name: Poisoner
description: Davokar hides many alchemically potent and poisonous plants, and the character is familiar with the effective use of poisoned weapons in combat. Poisons can be purchased from less scrupulous peddlers, but to actually brew a poison requires some understanding of alchemy (the Alchemy ability). The Poisoner ability can be used to identify different poisons or the effect of a poison on a wounded or dead person.
novice: [Free] Apply poison (1 dose/hit). Test [Cun←Str] for effect.
adept: [Free] Applied poison lasts for entire combat.
master: [Free] Test [Cun] to increase poison level. Strong gives 2nd chance on effect test.

name: Polearm mastery
description: The character is initiated in the secrets of longshafted weapons. The spear is a simple weapon and anyone can quickly learn how to make good use of its length. For this reason, the militia armies of the plains and forests are often armed with spears. The character's advanced skill with long weapons really shows that a simple shaft of hardened wood can be a fearsome weapon in the hands of a trained warrior.
novice: [Pas] Long weapon dmg +1 step (Spear/Halberd 1D10, Staff 1D8).
adept: [Rea] Free Attack against enemies entering melee (unless they have Long).
master: [Rea] If Free Attack hits, enemy stopped (cannot attack with melee).

name: Quick draw
description: Dealing the first blow can decide the outcome of a battle, and with this ability the character has an advantage when an unexpected ambush happens. The character also becomes a much more dynamic warrior, able to quickly switch weapons to meet the demands of any situation – a skill particularly appreciated among barbarian skirmishers and Ambrian archers.
novice: [Free] Test [Qui] to Draw/Reload as Free Action.
adept: [Free] Test [Qui] to switch weapons as Free Action.
master: [Free] Test [Qui] to use elixir on self/other as Free Action.

name: Recovery
description: Among both Black Cloaks and Mystics, meditative techniques that provide strange bodily capabilities have been developed. The character can use its inner power reserves with an almost magical self-discipline to rejuvenate the energy of its body, even when in the midst of combat.
novice: [Act] Test [Res] to regain 1D4 [Tgh]. Once/day.
adept: [Act] Regain 1D6 [Tgh].
master: [Act] Regain 1D8 [Tgh].

name: Ritualist
description: The character has learned how mystical powers can be channeled through rituals – powerful but time-consuming magical practices. This knowledge may come from studying under a teacher or from self-studies with a ritual codex. The character suffers one (1) permanent Corruption from each ritual it learns, except if the ritual belongs to a mystical tradition practiced by the character. In the latter case the character is spared the blight of Corruption. When it comes to performing rituals, the character suffers 1D4 temporary Corruption if the ritual does not belong to a tradition he or she has mastered. Performing rituals covered by the character's tradition only gives one (1) point of temporary Corruption. The Ritualist ability makes it possible for the character to recognize what ritual has been performed by examining symbols and components remaining on the scene, and also to deduce the effects of the ritual, even if he or she has not mastered it.
novice: [Spec] Learn 1 ritual. +1 Perm. Corr if not in tradition. 1D4 Temp. Corr/use (1 if tradition).
adept: [Spec] Learn +2 rituals (3 total).
master: [Spec] Learn +3 rituals (6 total).

name: Shield fighter
description: The character is trained in how to make good use of a shield, and how to actively fight using the shield as a weapon. Behind the protection of the shield, the character can generate a great momentum to fuel its attacks, as well as strike with the shield itself. This is an effective combination which probably explains why it is so common among both barbarian and Ambrian warriors. The buckler, the light shield usually utilized by archers, is too light to be used with the Shield Fighter ability. The warrior has to carry a sturdy shield made of either wood or steel to generate the required amount of force.
novice: [Pas] Weapon dmg +1 step (1H 1D10, Short 1D8). Shield Def bonus +2.
adept: [Rea] Shield Bash after hit (1D4 dmg). Knockdown if [Str←Str].
master: [Rea] Shield Bash 1D8 dmg. Knockdown if [Str←Str].

name: Sixth sense
description: When moving through dark forests and underground tunnels, one's eyes are no longer very useful. Lighting a lantern or torch may summon dangers, so the explorer had better learn to rely on his or her other senses. With dedicated training it is possible to awaken these other senses and sharpen them to the brink of eeriness. The Sixth Sense ability provides the character with unique capabilities when fighting at a distance or in situations where eyesight can no longer be trusted. A character with Sixth Sense may under calm circumstances navigate unhindered in dim light, as well as maintain a sense of direction in complete darkness, though at a pace of only a quarter of its normal, daytime speed.
novice: [Pas] Use [Vig] instead of [Acc] for Ranged.
adept: [Pas] Use [Vig] instead of [Qui] for Initiative/Defense.
master: [Pas] Move/Fight unhindered in darkness/blinded.

name: Sorcery
description: The character is one of those who are arrogant or desperate enough to cling to the darkness. While other mystical traditions do everything they can to avoid the soul-eroding powers of Corruption, the sorcerer chooses to do the opposite. The powers and rituals of Sorcery rely on the force of corruption and the possibilities offered by the taint. The sorcerer must always balance between grasping the black power that is just within its reach and remaining independent of the darkness. Most sorcerers realize that their chosen path only holds one possible end, and the most depraved among them have already come to terms with this, seeing their final and inevitable enslavement as some sort of salvation.
novice: [Spec] Test [Res] to take only 1 Temp. Corr.
adept: [Rea] Re-roll failed power test vs Total Corr. Success: Power works but +1D4 Temp. Corr.
master: [Spec] Test vs target's [Shadow] instead of [Res]. (Thoroughly Corrupt immune).

name: Steadfast
description: Mental disciplines and stratagems for resisting improper influences have been developed among the ranks of the Templars and Black Cloaks. Also among Mystics there are individuals who study the art of resistance. The character has a mind as hard as steel, inspiring it to fight on even against insurmountable odds. Mystics rarely succeed when trying to hurt or seize control of the character's senses, and sometimes a truly steadfast character manages to defend itself mentally and even turn the magic back on the hostile mystic.
novice: [Rea] 2nd chance on [Str]/[Res] vs physical effects (traps, poison, magic fire).
adept: [Rea] 2nd chance vs mind/senses effects.
master: [Rea] Failed mental attack vs character deals 1D6 dmg (ign. Armor) to attacker.

name: Steel throw
description: There are traditions and groups whose representatives have practiced the art of the thrown weapon for generations. Throwing knives are for instance common among thieves and thugs in the cities, and in the woods many clan warriors are equipped with throwing axes or spears. In fact, most barbarian fighters (especially those within the clan of Zarek) regularly use throwing weapons as part of their combat tactics, unleashing a shower of steel just before they charge into the fray.
novice: [Pas] Throwing weapon dmg 1D8.
adept: [Act] Double throw (separate rolls). Can throw melee weapons (base dmg).
master: [Act] Triple throw.

name: Strangler
description: The character has been initiated into the dirty, but sometimes necessary, art of strangulation. This fighting technique has a bad reputation among Ambrians and barbarians alike, but that does not mean that it is not widely desired by those who want enemies or their guards discreetly taken care of. With this ability the character can do a lot of damage to an unprepared or slow enemy with either a garrote or, if more advanced, with the alchemical Choking Spores.
novice: [Act] Advantage attack deals 1D6/turn (ign. Armor). Maintain with [Cun←Cun]. Target immobilized.
adept: [Act] Test [Cun←Qui] to use Choking Spores. 1D4 dmg/turn for 1D4 turns (ign. Armor).
master: [Act] Use Spore Bomb (Area). [Cun] to hit. 1D4 dmg/turn for 1D4 turns (ign. Armor).

name: Tactician
description: According to Ambrians, scholarly knowledge is counted as one of the highest virtues. Hence, it is hardly surprising that Ambrian scholars have studied skirmishes meticulously to see if the tactics of battles can work on a lesser scale, among smaller groups and even in duels. The result is a style of combat governed by strict principles and calculations, which over time can out-maneuver even the most aggressive attacker. The character is trained in this scholarly warrior tradition. A schooled tactician may also use this ability to analyze a tactical approach and find both its strengths and weaknesses. This can be done for offensive purposes when facing a hostile group or defensively, to establish a strong defense.
novice: [Pas] Use [Cun] instead of [Qui] for Initiative.
adept: [Pas] Use [Cun] instead of [Qui] for Defense.
master: [Pas] Use [Cun] instead of [Acc] for Attacks (except Heavy).

name: Theurgy
description: Theurgy is the mystical tradition championed by the chosen priest mages of the Church of Prios. Theurgy is the doctrine of the inner flame, where the ember of the soul is seen as a reflection of the divine and life-giving light of the sun.
novice: [Spec] No Perm. Corr for Novice Theurgy powers/rituals.
adept: [Spec] No Perm. Corr for Adept Theurgy. 1 Temp. Corr/use.
master: [Spec] +1D4 healing/holy dmg. No Perm. Corr for Master Theurgy.

name: Twin attack
description: Barbarians, Ambrians and goblins all have fighting techniques involving the use of more than one weapon. The character has learned how to fight with two weapons, an advanced but effective technique that gives the warrior an offensive advantage. Twin Attack is especially effective against lightly armored targets.
novice: [Act] Attack twice (1D8 & 1D6). +1 Def if dual wielding.
adept: [Act] Attack twice (1D8 each).
master: [Act] Attack twice (1D10 & 1D8).

name: Two-handed force
description: The knights of Ambria as well as the Wrathguards of Karvosti dress themselves in steel from head to toe and have realized that with that much armor, they are free to focus on dealing massive amounts of damage. Heavy two-handed weapons rest comfortably in the character's callused hands and can have an astoundingly destructive effect on all sorts of targets. Heavy weapons are extra effective against heavily armored enemies.
novice: [Pas] Heavy weapon dmg 1D12.
adept: [Rea] Missed attack triggers re-roll (1D8 dmg).
master: [Act] Heavy attacks ign. Armor.

name: Witchcraft
description: From the deep soils and wild spirits of Davokar comes the tradition of witchcraft. For generations, its teachings have been passed on to witches who, alongside the chieftains, have led the people of the forests through mishaps and triumphs alike. Surely, it is the primal powers of witchcraft that enables the barbarian clans to live within Davokar.
novice: [Spec] No Perm. Corr for Novice Witchcraft powers/rituals.
adept: [Spec] No Perm. Corr for Adept Witchcraft. 1 Temp. Corr/use.
master: [Spec] No Perm. Corr for Master Witchcraft.

name: Witchsight
description: By way of the shadows surrounding creatures, locations and objects the world's deeper conflicts are observable for a character with the Witchsight ability. Opening up one's mind in order to examine the world of shadows can provide invaluable insights, but it also entails great risk: the more open the mind is and the deeper the insights are, the greater the risk of becoming tainted by the darkness of the world. It is for this reason that masters of this ability seldom use it to their full capacity. As previously stated, the color of the Shadows can give the character clues regarding the spiritual alliance of the inspected creature (see Shadow & Corruption, page 174). The Game Master manages the nuances and powers of the Shadows and describes what the character sees with its Witchsight.
novice: [Free] Test [Vig←Dis] to see Dominant Shadow. 1 Temp. Corr.
adept: [Free] See all Shadows (not strength). 1D4 Temp. Corr.
master: [Free] See all Shadows & strengths. 1D6 Temp. Corr.

name: Wizardry
description: Wizardry is taught by Ordo Magica and is a tradition whose practitioners are well-versed in the mysteries of fire, the will's triumph over matter and the labyrinths of the senses. To wizards of the Order, these phenomena are intimately connected.
novice: [Spec] No Perm. Corr for Novice Wizardry powers/rituals.
adept: [Spec] No Perm. Corr for Adept Wizardry. 1 Temp. Corr/use.
master: [Spec] Re-roll 1 failed Chain test/turn. No Perm. Corr for Master Wizardry.

name: Agile combat
description: During combat in wooded areas and hilly terrain the distance between opponents can shift quickly, from ranged to melee...
novice: [Pas] Split Movement Action before & after Combat Action. Provokes Free Attacks as normal.
adept: [Pas] Switch weapons as part of Combat Action.
master: [Rea] 2nd chance on [Def] vs Free Attacks from withdrawing. Success gives Free Attack (can switch weapon).

name: Armored mystic
description: The templars have developed techniques for performing the miracles of Prios while wearing full armor...
novice: [Pas] Medium armor doesn't affect powers ([Def] penalty remains).
adept: [Pas] Heavy armor doesn't affect powers ([Def] penalty remains).
master: [Pas] Armor grants +1D4 bonus protection.

name: Arrow jab
description: In the chaos of the battlefield, archers sometimes find themselves dragged into the melee...
novice: [Rea] Melee attack with arrow/bolt. Deals 1D6 dmg.
adept: [Rea] As Novice, deals 1D8 dmg.
master: [Rea] As Adept + Free Attack with bow/crossbow if jab hits.

name: Artifact crafting
description: The character is trained in the art of artifact crafting and can create artifacts of the lower order...
novice: [Spec] Once/adventure, test [Cun] to craft Novice artifact.
adept: [Spec] Test [Cun] to craft Adept artifact.
master: [Spec] Test [Cun] to craft Master artifact.

name: Axe artist
description: By tradition, many warriors of barbarian origin carry axes into battle, and among these fighters special techniques have been developed...
novice: [Act] Strike with short end. 1D6 dmg. Stun (Free Attack) if [Acc←Res] passed.
adept: [Act] Double-strike (two attacks at 1D8 dmg).
master: [Pas] Axe deals +1D4 dmg (1 hit/action).

name: Blacksmith
description: All peoples in Ambria and Davokar have their blacksmiths, which says something about their importance...
novice: [Spec] Test [Cun] to craft Novice item (Short/Long only).
adept: [Spec] Test [Cun] to craft Adept item (1 quality).
master: [Spec] Test [Cun] to craft Master item (multiple/mystical qualities).

name: Blood combat
description: The witches on Karvosti understand the power of the blood better than others...
novice: [Rea] If [Tgh] halved, 2nd chance on melee attacks.
adept: [Rea] If [Tgh] halved, melee deals +1D8 dmg.
master: [Rea] Heal [Tgh] equal to half melee dmg dealt.

name: Channeling
description: Some sorcerers and cultists have through exposure to dark powers developed a capacity to endure corruption...
novice: [Rea] Take Temp. Corr intended for another.
adept: [Rea] 2nd chance on Corruption rolls (take favorable).
master: [Rea] Test [Res←Res] to transfer Corruption to target. Fail: take half, surroundings take rest.

name: Cheap shot
description: In the slums of Alberetor's larger cities, special techniques for self-defense emerged...
novice: [Act] Unarmed attack 1D6 dmg. Hit grants Free Attack.
adept: [Rea] If melee hits, test [Cun←Qui] to knockdown.
master: [Rea] Riposte on enemy engaging. 1D6 dmg (ign. Armor).

name: Ensnare
description: Using weapons like bolas, nets or the long whip, many fighters and hunters of barbarian origin learn to limit the movement of enemies or prey...
novice: [Act] 2nd chance to ensnare (requires Ensnaring weapon).
adept: [Act] 2nd chance to knockdown ensnared enemy.
master: [Rea] Ensnare strangles: 1D6 dmg/turn (ign. Armor). Can choke unconscious.

name: Feat of strength
description: The warrior's spirit is strengthened in combat, giving him or her miraculous power when needed...
novice: [Pas] [Tgh] counts as [Str + 5].
adept: [Rea] If [Tgh] halved, 2nd chance on [Str] tests.
master: [Rea] If [Tgh] halved, deal +1D4 melee dmg.

name: Flailer
description: Among Ambria's knights and their squires, the efficiency of jointed chain-weapons has long been known...
novice: [Pas] Jointed weapons gain Ensnaring quality.
adept: [Pas] Jointed secondary dmg increases to 1D8.
master: [Act] If attack hits, make attacks against all enemies in range.

name: Hammer rhythm
description: As a weapon, the hammer is ancient and its brutal simplicity may in the right hands pound forth a deadly rhythm...
novice: [Rea] If enemy parries with shield, test [Str←Qui] to break/disarm shield + 1D6 dmg.
adept: [Rea] If enemy defends, test [Str←Str] to push back & Free Attack.
master: [Act] Two attacks on same target. Can push back (as Adept) if blocked.

name: Hunter's instinct
description: Hunters have a finely tuned instinct and when it comes down to it there are few targets...
novice: [Spec] Appoint target. 2nd chance on ranged attacks vs target.
adept: [Pas] Ranged vs appointed target +1D4 dmg.
master: [Rea] Free Ranged Attack when appointed target moves.

name: Knife play
description: The use of knives is common in the slums of Yndaros; short blades have advantages when fighting in narrow alleys...
novice: [Pas] Use [Qui] instead of [Acc] with knife.
adept: [Pas] Double attack with knife (main hand).
master: [Rea] Knife dmg puts enemy at 'short range'. Enemy must win Init or withdraw to use long weapons.

name: Mantle dance
description: Among Ambria's fencers, shields are regarded as awkward and barbaric, making the parrying dagger a more fashionable tool for defense...
novice: [Pas] Mantle in free hand gives +1 Def.
adept: [Act] Blind enemy with mantle. Hit grants Free Attack vs blinded target.
master: [Act] Mantle gains Ensnaring quality.

name: Opportunist
description: In the midst of battle, weak spots are exposed and can be exploited...
novice: [Rea] 2nd chance on Free Attacks from withdrawal.
adept: [Rea] Can use active abilities on withdrawal Free Attacks (loses 2nd chance).
master: [Rea] Gain both 2nd chance AND active abilities on withdrawal Free Attacks.

name: Pyrotechnics
description: In Ambria, advances within the field of alchemy have led to the use of alchemical weapons...
novice: [Act] Use Flash Powder ([Acc←Qui], 1D4 dmg, blind). Safe grenade handling.
adept: [Act] Use Smoke Bomb (blind area, poison dmg). Safe fire tube handling.
master: [Act] Use Thunder Ball (Area, 1D12 dmg, blind). Massive quality for weapons.

name: Rapid fire
description: Archers in Ambria and Davokar have developed techniques for rapid firing...
novice: [Act] Sacrifice Move to fire 2 arrows.
adept: [Act] Fire 2 arrows in one Combat Action.
master: [Act] Fire 3 arrows in one Combat Action.

name: Rapid reflexes
description: Rogues do not have much in common, besides that they all are survivalists...
novice: [Rea] Take half dmg instead of full, or zero instead of half (from area/grenades).
adept: [Rea] Pass [Def] to switch places with attacker (avoid flank).
master: [Pas] Act first in turn order (unless rival has ability + higher stat).

name: Rune tattoo
description: The rune crafters of Clan Vajvod in eastern Davokar often tattoo themselves and their allies with powerful runes...
novice: [Rea] Activate for +1D4 Armor. Costs 1 Temp. Corr/hit.
adept: [Free] Regenerate 1 [Tgh]/turn. Costs 1 Temp. Corr/point.
master: [Rea] Deal +1D4 dmg. Costs 1 Temp. Corr/hit.

name: Siege expert
description: In Ambria, wars are fought in two ways: on the battlefield and through sieges. Siege weapons are used in both cases...
novice: [Spec] Use ballista, build siege towers. Safe grenade handling.
adept: [Spec] Use catapult/trebuchet. Dig trenches. Use smoke/breaching/fire tubes.
master: [Spec] Alchemical weapons gain Massive quality.

name: Staff fighting
description: The apparent simplicity of the staff tends to mask its versatility as a weapon...
novice: [Pas] +1 Def with Long weapon (+2 with Staff).
adept: [Rea] Free Attack (1D6 dmg) if enemy defends against your attack. (Staff: also if you defend).
master: [Act] Test [Acc←Qui] to trip enemy + Free Attack.

name: Staff magic
description: The staff mages were once the guards of the Symbarian emperor...
novice: [Spec] Staff absorbs Novice Corr. Elemental rune deals +1D4 dmg.
adept: [Spec] Staff absorbs Adept Corr. 2nd chance on Corruption rolls (take lower).
master: [Spec] Staff absorbs Master Corr. No Temp. Corr for Staff Magic powers.

name: Strong gift
description: There are many myths describing the origin of mystical powers, and all established traditions are quick to state that theirs is the oldest...
novice: [Spec] Choose signature power/ritual. Costs 1 Temp. Corr.
adept: [Pas] Corr Threshold = full [Res]. Blight born at [Res]x2.
master: [Spec] Cast ANY power at Novice level. 2nd chance to fail test. 1D8 Temp. Corr.

name: Sword saint
description: Among Ambria's duelists, there are those who have achieved an almost mystic symbiosis with their fencing swords...
novice: [Pas] 1H Sword dmg 1D10 (with parrying dagger).
adept: [Rea] Free Attack after successful Def (once/turn).
master: [Rea] Unlimited Free Attacks after Def. 1H Sword dmg 1D12.

name: Symbolism
description: Symbolism was developed in the east, beyond the Ravens, in what the symbolists call “The first city of humans”...
novice: [Spec] Create symbol (1 hr). Activate [Act] (touch/sight). 1 symbol/power.
adept: [Spec] Draw temp symbol [Act]. Activate [Free] or by Trigger.
master: [Act] Draw & activate in air. 1 Temp. Corr. No prep limit.

name: Trapper
description: Traps have been used since ancient times and in Davokar they are particularly useful...
novice: [Act] Deploy/disarm mechanical traps [Cun]. Improvised trap 1D6 dmg.
adept: [Act] Handle alchemical mines. Improvised trap 1D8 dmg.
master: [Act] Traps +1 tier. 2nd chance on Strong traps. Dmg rolled twice (take high). Improvised 1D10.

name: Trick archery
description: Trick shooting with bows and crossbows is highest fashion in Ambria, as appreciated at shows as it is effective in combat...
novice: [Act] Full turn to disarm/pin/blind enemy (if dmg dealt). Target loses action.
adept: [Act] Ricochet shot to hit covered/hidden target.
master: [Rea] Test [Acc←Qui] to parry ranged attack or melee on ally.

name: Troll singing
description: The mystical tradition of trolls is expressed through singing, sometimes accompanied by music played on horn, flute or pipes...
novice: [Spec] No Perm. Corr for Novice songs. 2nd chance on social/mind tests (once/scene).
adept: [Spec] No Perm. Corr for Adept songs. Re-roll 1 social/mind test/chain.
master: [Spec] No Perm. Corr for Master songs. Re-roll all social/mind tests.

name: Wrestling
description: Wrestling is popular among warriors, appreciated for educational purposes as well as its entertainment value...
novice: [Act] Grapple with weapon. [Str←Str] to throw (1D4 dmg) or hold.
adept: [Rea] After Def, test [Qui←Str] to throw attacker (1D4 dmg + stun).
master: [Rea] Throw attacker [Qui←Str] without Def test. 1D6 dmg + stun + Free Attack.

name: Harsh Rebuke
description: Words can have as much impact as a strike upon the cheek or a whack upon the shield...
novice: [Pas] 2nd chance on social tests.
adept: [Rea] Test [Per←Res] to stop target's action (unless defending life).
master: [Act] Test [Per←Res] to deal 1 Resolute dmg.

name: Incremental Ritualist
description: Ritualist is an Incremental Ability. You cannot buy the Ritualist ability directly with Experience. Instead, you advance the level of your Ritualist ability by learning new rituals...
novice: [Spec] Know 1 ritual. Identify ritual signs.
adept: [Spec] Know 3 rituals. Identify rituals from studied traditions.
master: [Spec] Know 6 rituals. Identify any ritual. [Res] to learn specific details.

name: Parry Mastery
novice: [Pas] Use [Acc] for Defense in melee.
adept: [Rea] After successful Def, test [Acc←Str] to disarm.
master: [Pas] Use [Acc] for Defense vs Ranged. Catch projectile if Natural Warrior.

name: Alchemy (Revised)
description: The character is schooled in the mysteries of alchemy. They spend their time cooking together strange elixirs and mystical concoctions to help themselves and their allies brave the dangers of Davokar...
novice: [Spec] Test [Cun] for 1 Novice elixir (or random on fail).
adept: [Spec] Test [Cun] for 1 Adept or 1D4 Novice elixirs.
master: [Spec] Test [Cun] for 1 Master, 1D4 Adept, or 1D6 Novice elixirs.

name: Anathema
description: The mystic has studied the secrets of countering magic and can dispel the effects of other powers. Anathema does not affect rituals – their mystical bonds are too thoroughly woven and can only be dispelled by other rituals.
novice: [Act] Test [Res←Res] to dispel ongoing power on self or creature.
adept: [Act] Dispel multiple targets in a Chain (test for each).
master: [Act] Test [Res] to dispel all mystical effects, summoned creatures, etc.

name: Bend will
description: Free will is an illusion, but the power of the will isunmistakable. The mystic has come to understandthese seemingly contradictory principles and canuse the insight to control the will of other creatures.
novice: [Act] Test [Res←Res] to control creature (1 action/turn, no actives). Break on conc. loss or failed test.
adept: [Act] Sustained (no concentration needed). Ends on failed [Res←Res].
master: [Act] Controlled creature performs 2 actions/turn.

name: Blessed shield
description: By faith and will, the mystic raises a holy shield against the weapons of its enemies. The shield is invisible until attacked, at which time it glitters as if struck by sunlight.
novice: [Act] Test [Res] for +1D4 Armor. Deals 1D4 dmg to abom/undead attackers (ign. Armor). Lasts for Scene.
adept: [Act] +1D6 Armor/Dmg. Include 1 ally.
master: [Act] +1D8 Armor/Dmg. Include 2 allies.

name: Brimstone cascade
description: The mystic can unleash the rampaging spirit of fire and burn its enemies to cinders, or at least scorch them severely.
novice: [Act] Test [Res←Qui]. Success: 1D12 dmg. Fail: 1D6 dmg.
adept: [Act] Chain on full dmg (1D12). Arcs to next target until test fails.
master: [Act] Chain continues on failed test (1D6). Stops after 2nd failure.

name: Confusion
description: The mystic's understanding of the labyrinth of the senses can cause an enemy to lose iteself inside its own mind. Confused enemies become paralyzed o rlose their ability to separate friend from foe.
novice: [Act] Test [Res←Res]. Target paralyzed or attacks random neighbor. Check each turn.
adept: [Act] Sustained (no concentration needed). Test [Res←Res] each turn.
master: [Act] Creates Chain of Confusion.

name: Curse
description: The mystic masters the stare of the Evil Eye and can curse enemies on the battlefield; a power often used by the disciples of the Dark Lords during The Great War.
novice: [Free] 1/turn, enemy gets 2nd chance to fail tests vs mystic.
adept: [Free] Enemy gets 2nd chance to fail ALL tests.
master: [Act] Enemy takes 1D6 dmg (ign. Armor) per action taken. Safe if passive.

name: Entangling vines
description: The earth is bound by roots, while objects above ground are often covered by vines. All that the mystic does is uses its will to stimulate the already ongoing processes of nature.
novice: [Act] Test [Res]. Ensnare enemy (no move). Break on failed [Res←Str].
adept: [Act] Creates Chain of ensnarement.
master: [Act] Chain + Ensnared take 1D6 dmg/turn (ign. Armor).

name: Flame wall
description: The mystic has gained insights into the mysteries of fire and can summon fire to form it into a wall or a dome.
novice: [Act] Test [Res]. Wall deals 1D12 fire dmg if passed. Auto-dmg if summoned on line of enemies.
adept: [Act] Ring of fire. Encircle self/allies/enemies.
master: [Act] Dome of fire. Covers self/allies/enemies.

name: Holy aura
description: The mystic can send out a holy and life-affirming aura that harms abominations and the undead. At higher levels, this aura can also provide healing powers for living creatures.
novice: [Act] Test [Res]. 1D6 dmg to abom/undead (ign. Armor). Ongoing.
adept: [Act] 1D8 dmg + Living heal 1D4/turn.
master: [Act] 1D10 dmg + Living heal 1D6/turn.

name: Illusory correction
description: There is a gap between the world and the perception of it. The mystic can use this gap to evade a potentially horrible fate or to make alterations to the flow and perception of reality.
novice: [Rea] Test [Res] to re-roll failed [Def].
adept: [Rea] Test [Res] to re-roll any test affecting mystic.
master: [Rea] Test [Res] to re-roll any test affecting target.

name: Inherit wound
description: The mystic has closely studied the spirits of creation and death, and can use this knowledge to redistribute damage between itself, its allies and its enemies.
novice: [Free] Test [Res]. Target heals 1D6, mystic takes equal dmg.
adept: [Free] Heals 1D8. Mystic inherits poison/bleeding + takes half dmg.
master: [Act] Target heals 1D8. Mystic takes half dmg, passes half to enemy (ign. Armor).

name: Larvae boil
description: Drawing from the force of wrath the mystic can infuse an enemy's body with larvae that then start to eat their way out. Although it is loudly refuted by members of the court, persistent rumors say that this is how the hero king Ynedar met his demise.
novice: [Act] 1D4 dmg/turn (ign. Armor). Ends on failed [Res←Str].
adept: [Act] 1D6 dmg/turn (ign. Armor).
master: [Act] 1D8 dmg/turn (ign. Armor).

name: Lay on hands
description: The secrets of life lay bare for the mystic and with them follows the coveted power of healing, often interpreted as a gift from whichever deity the mystic adheres to.
novice: [Act] Touch & Test [Res] to heal 1D6 [Tgh]. Works on self.
adept: [Act] Heals 1D8 [Tgh] and cures poison/bleeding.
master: [Act] Ranged healing (sight). Heals 1D8 [Tgh] + cures poison/bleeding. Touch healing increases to 1D12 [Tgh].

name: Levitate
description: The binding force of the world can be manipulated, and with that insight the mystic has gained the capability to levitate, using nothing but the power of the mind.
novice: [Act] Test [Res]. Fly 1 stride/turn. Fall deals 1D6 (ign. Armor).
adept: [Act] Fly ally [Res←Str]. Fall deals 1D6 (ign. Armor).
master: [Act] Fly Chain of allies [Res←Str]. Fall deals no dmg.

name: Maltransformation
description: The mystic has grasped that physical appearance is a dynamic concept, and knows how to use that insight to transform its enemies into weaker forms.
novice: [Act] Test [Res]. Turn target into harmless beast. Sustained by [Res←Res] each turn. Target keeps Attributes but loses abilities/items.
adept: [Act] Ongoing effect. No concentration needed. Ends on failed [Res←Res] test.
master: [Act] Creates Chain of transformations. Ongoing until [Res] test fails (check per target/turn).

name: Mind-throw
description: The mystic can use its mind to move and throw loose objects, or even enemies.
novice: [Act] Throw object [Res←Qui] 1D8 dmg. [Rea] Block with object ([Res←Acc/Res]).
adept: [Act] Throw enemy [Res←Str] (1D8 dmg + prone).
master: [Act] Throw Chain of enemies.

name: Nature's embrace
description: The deep soil of the world is a safe place for the mystic, just as the mountain rock may become a shelter. The mystic can sink into the earth and thereby avoid attacks from its enemies.
novice: [Act] Test [Res]. Sink into earth (invulnerable, no actions). Test [Res] each turn to stay.
adept: [Act] Cast on self while hidden. No test to stay.
master: [Act] Move underground. Cast on allies/see allies.

name: Prios' burning glass
description: The mystic can focus the light of its soul into a burning ray, which damages most beings and destroys the unholy.
novice: [Act] Test [Res]. 1D6 dmg (1D8 vs abom/undead).
adept: [Act] 1D8 dmg (1D12) to all enemies in sight.
master: [Act] 1D8 dmg (1D12) area + Stun corrupt/undead [Res←Res].

name: Revenant strike
description: The mystic's weapon is touched by dark energies, which increases the damage dealt against living creatures. Worse, those slain will rise again, as walking corpses controlled by the sorcerer. Undead created by revenant strikes have the same statistics as the dragoul (see page 230). The undead returns to its state of true death at the end of the scene.
novice: [Act] +1D4 dmg for Scene.
adept: [Rea] As Novice + Slain rise as undead servants.
master: [Free] As Adept + 1D8 dmg.

name: Shapeshift
description: The mystic's understanding of the essence of nature makes it possible to take the form of beasts – a talent that the snake witches of clan Gaoia are particularly renowned for.
novice: [Act] Test [Res]. Become small beast (scout). Re-roll [Dis]/[Qui] & Def. No Free Atk vs mystic.
adept: [Act] Battle beast (Armored I, Natural Weapon I).
master: [Act] Impressive battle beast (Regeneration I, Robust I).

name: Storm arrow
description: The mystic can ask the wind to lift and carry arrows towards its enemies. The barbarian witch Yagaba, a friend of Lasifor Nightpitch, sometimes demonstrates this power, and is rarely seen without a handful of black-feathered arrows floating by her side.
novice: [Act] Test [Res]. 5 arrows float. Fire [Free] (1/turn). Auto-hit 1D6.
adept: [Act] 1D8 dmg. Fire 2/action (lose Free Fire).
master: [Act] Fire 3/action (lose Free Fire).

name: True form
description: The mystic has spent many long nights closely studying lies and false guises, and is capable of making the surrounding world reveal its true nature.
novice: [Rea] Test [Res←Res] to see through illusions/transformations.
adept: [Act] Force Chain of creatures to true form.
master: [Act] Force true form & prevent shift (Test [Res] on attempt).

name: Unholy aura
description: The mystic can surround itself with an aura of unholy energies that harms living enemies but heals abominations and undead.
novice: [Act] Test [Res]. 1D6 dmg to living (ign. Armor). Ongoing.
adept: [Act] Exclude living allies from dmg.
master: [Act] 1D8 dmg + Heal undead/abom 1D8.

name: Unnoticeable
description: The mystic can remain undetected by subtly turning the enemy's attention elsewhere.
novice: [Act] Test [Res←Res]. Invisible to one target. Breaks on atk/dmg.
adept: [Act] Test [Res]. Invisible to all nearby enemies.
master: [Act] Invisible self & one ally (separately).

name: Witch hammer
description: Sanctifying Rite. The mystic has learned to shroud its melee weapon with holy and blight-hating fire, just like the legendary Light bringer Ofelya Attio.
novice: [Free] Weapon deals +1D4 dmg (+1D6 vs abom/undead). Scene.

name: Banishing seal
description: The mystic binds banishing energies to a symbol, that when unleashed sweeps out in waves over the area. Upon creation, the mystic must choose what type of creature will be affected (Abominations, Beasts, Cultural Beings or Undead).
novice: [Act] Chain banish [Res←Res] (leave scene). Choose type.
adept: [Act] Unaffected take 1D4 dmg (ign. Armor).
master: [Act] Unaffected take 1D8 dmg (ign. Armor).

name: Black bolt
description: During The Great War, the black bolts of the Dark Lords, ensnaring and burning their targets, were feared by all. In more recent days, other sorcerers have discovered that they can do the same, by extending their tainted souls and using them as a whip that traps and corrodes the enemy. The mystic cannot cast a new black bolt as long as at least one enemy is ensnared by the power, but he or she is free to make use of other mystical powers.
novice: [Act] Test [Res←Qui]. 1D6 dmg (ign. Armor) + Trapped. Break [Res] or conc. loss.
adept: [Act] Creates Chain. All break free if one succeeds.
master: [Act] Chain. Targets must break free individually.

name: Black breath
description: A mystic with permanent corruption can spew out its inner darkness and infect others with corruption, or heal already tainted creatures.
novice: [Act] Roll 1D4 vs Total Corr. Low: Heal [Tgh]. High: Take Temp. Corr.
adept: [Act] Roll 1D6 vs Total Corr.
master: [Act] Chain (1D6). Stops on heal.

name: Blinding Symbol
description: Intricate runes emit energies that can temporarily blind those who are bedazzled by the light. The effect of a Blinding Symbol is immediately suspended if the victim uses a dose of Eye Drops.
novice: [Act] Chain blind [Res←Res] (1 turn).
adept: [Act] Blind sustained until conc. loss or [Res] fail.
master: [Act] Blind permanent until healed.

name: Combat hymn
description: There is a raw and untamed power in singing, and some mystics learn to sing while fighting to gain considerable extra strength when battling the enemy. The character is one of those who have learned to sing combat hymns to increase his or her chances in combat. The song is interrupted if the mystic uses another mystical power or if concentration is lost due to taking damage [Resolute –Damage].
novice: [Free] Group +1 to [Qui], [Str] or [Acc] (sustained).
adept: [Free] Group +1 to ALL three.
master: [Free] Group +1 to ALL + Heal 1D6 (once/scene).

name: Dancing weapon
description: By willpower alone, the mystic makes a weapon soar and fight, with the speed and agility of a thought. The weapon in question does not have to be special in any way; if it has qualities or powers, these may be used by the mystic according to standard rules of combat. However, the mystic cannot use other abilities related to melee combat while using this power.
novice: [Act] Use [Res] for Atk/Def. No other powers/abilities while active.
adept: [Act] Weapon fights independently. Mystic free to act.
master: [Free] Weapon activates/defends automatically.

name: Draining glyph
description: The mystic creates a glyph that upon activation becomes a whirling vortex, sucking the life-force from the enemy. The glyph affects all enemies who can see the symbol and are in front of it.
novice: [Act] Test [Res←Str]. 1D4 dmg (ign. Armor) to all in front. Sustained.
adept: [Act] Sustained (no conc. loss from dmg).
master: [Act] Heal 1D4 [Tgh]/turn from drained energy.

name: Exorcize
description: A Sorcerer's lack of respect for the laws of nature lends him or her the astounding ability to tear at and bend apparent constants like time and space. One way to make use of this is to temporarily banish creatures from the world of the living, out into the Yonderworld where alien winds howl in chorus with hunting abominations. This poses a danger for the demonologist, since every failed attempt to use the power risks bringing an abomination into the world. If this happens, the abomination attacks a random victim, though not someone who is protected by an Unholy Aura or whose soul is already thoroughly corrupt. The abomination that comes has an equal chance (1d6) of being (1–2) a Vindictive Daemon, 3–4) a Knowledgeable Daemon, or (5–6) a Guardian Daemon (for stats, see the ritual Summon Daemon on page 94).
novice: [Act] [Res←Res] send enemy to Yonderworld (1 turn). 1D4 dmg (ign. Armor) + Corr. Fail = Abomination enters.
adept: [Act] Sustained. 1D4 dmg/Corr per turn. Risk Abomination each turn/on fail.
master: [Rea] 1/turn, Banish attacker [Res←Res].

name: Fire soul
description: Pyromancers have found that those who dedicate their lives to the study of fire in time learn to instinctively use it as a shield and a weapon. It is even said that the most devoted learn to manipulate the force of hostile fires and paradoxically enough use these burning powers to heal themselves when wounded.
novice: [Rea] 1D6 fire dmg to melee attacker. +1D6 Armor vs fire.
adept: [Rea] 1D10 dmg & Armor.
master: [Rea] Fire heals half dmg. Retaliate at range (1D10).

name: Heroic hymn
description: There is power in the heroic hymns of old. The mystic can sing while fighting, thereby filling his or her allies with courage and vigor. The song is interrupted if the mystic uses another mystical power or if concentration is lost by taking damage [Resolute –Damage].
novice: [Free] Group +1 to [Cun], [Res] or [Per] (sustained).
adept: [Free] Group +1 to ALL three.
master: [Free] Group +1 to ALL + Reduce Temp. Corr 1D4 (once/scene).

name: Lifegiver
description: The wellspring of life runs clear and refreshing in these dark days. Dedicated healers can draw from its power and transform it into a purifying gift that cleanses souls of corruption and heals physical wounds.
novice: [Act] Remove 1D4 Temp. Corr from target. Excess heals [Tgh]. Works on self.
adept: [Act] Remove 1D4 Temp. Corr from group.
master: [Rea] Group reduces Temp. Corr gained by 1D4 (passive).

name: Mirroring
description: Reality's layers of misconceptions and lies may be used to project a series of conceivable phenomena, only one of which corresponds to the reality of the world. The multiple false images created this way serve to protect the mystic from hostile attacks – in most cases; there is always the risk that the enemy targets the mystic instead of an illusion. Every attack against the mystic has a chance of hitting one of the projections or the mystic: if three illusions are made, the chance of the mystic being targeted is 1 out of 4. As the illusions are destroyed, the mystic's risk of being hit increases.
novice: [Act] Test [Res]. Create 1D4 copies. Hit destroys copy. Area dmg dispels all.
adept: [Act] 1D6 copies. Area dmg dispels 1 copy.
master: [Act] 1D8 copies. Area dmg dispels 0 copies.

name: Protective runes
description: The mystic's runes emit protective energies that surround the mystic and at higher levels also punish his or her ennemies.
novice: [Act] +1D4 Armor (stacks). Sustained.
adept: [Act] +1D4 Armor + 1D4 retal dmg (ign. Armor).
master: [Act] 1D6 Armor/Dmg.

name: Psychic thrust
description: Some mystics know how to project their will to form a psychic weapon that can attack the enemy together with the mystic's ordinary melee attacks. This means that the enemy must defend on two fronts, and risk failing at both. There is also a chance that the enemy will be paralyzed or severely damaged by the psychic thrust.
novice: [Rea] 2nd chance on melee attack test.
adept: [Rea] Test [Res←Res] to auto-hit.
master: [Rea] Auto-hit + 1D4 extra dmg (ign. Armor).

name: Purgatory
description: Blackened souls echo with pain and darkness, and a trained Inquisitor can use that darkness against the enemy, or even drown the twisted target in its own inner blackness.
novice: [Act] Roll 1D20 vs Total Corr. Low: Incap 1 turn. Thoroughly Corrupt: 1D6 dmg (ign. Armor).
adept: [Act] All enemies in sight.
master: [Rea] Enemies taking Corr take equal physical dmg (ign. Armor).

name: Retribution
description: Some dark-minded mystics can use their anger and vindictiveness to amass dark energies around a creature they want to hurt. In fact, at the higher levels the effect of this ability becomes instinctive, and all pain that the mystic suffers will undoubtedly be transferred to any enemies in the vicinity. Note that members of the race Dwarf can learn Retribution as if it was a normal ability. Hence, they suffer no corruption from using this particular power, neither when they learn it, nor when they make use of it. This pertains only to this power and the dwarven race.
novice: [Act] Test [Res←Res]. Attackers get 2nd chance to fail vs target.
adept: [Rea] Test [Res←Res]. Link dmg taken to attacker (1 link).
master: [Rea] Link multiple attackers.

name: Sphere
description: The mystic has his or her staff – or another melee weapon – spin around at such velocity that it forms a protective sphere. The sphere effectively parries most attacks. On the negative side, the mystic cannot perform attacks or use other powers without dispelling the sphere. The sphere is active until it is willingly aborted, until the mystic uses another power or until it is dispelled by some other mystic using the power Anathema.
novice: [Act] Use [Res] for Def. Move only. Blocks melee/ranged.
adept: [Act] Auto-defend vs wpn attacks (unlimited). Vulnerable to magic/area.
master: [Act] Cast on ally/hands free (use items/scrolls).

name: Spirit walk
description: Because of his or her closeness to death, the mystic has developed the mystical skill to assume the immaterial form of a spirit. Spirit Walk is hindered by Magic Circle, Witch Circle and Sanctifying Rite; the mystic cannot pass through or leave such areas while moving in the form of a spirit; however, it is possible to assume the spirit form when inside such protected domains. The Spirit Walk also ends if someone lights a Ghost Candle close by (see the alchemical elixir with that name, on page 153 in the Core Rulebook).
novice: [Act] Test [Res]. Move as spirit (ignore attacks/walls). 1 move/turn.
adept: [Rea] Negate hit [Res-Dmg]. Magic deals half.
master: [Rea] Attack bypasses Armor.

name: Staff projectile
description: In the hands of a staff mage, the rune staff is a powerful throwing weapon. The staff is thrown at an enemy and returns to the mystic's hand, whether it hits or not.
novice: [Act] Throw staff [Res] 1D8 dmg. Return.
adept: [Act] 1D10 dmg. Ignore cover/LoS.
master: [Act] Chain 1D12->1D10->... (max 5).

name: Teleport
description: The sorcerers who have gone furthest in questioning the laws of nature can tear holes in the world and step outside, only to tear another rift in the fabric of the Yonderworld and reenter the world of the living in a new location. As always when the shell of reality is perforated, there is a risk that an abomination slips through and attacks a random creature – except those protected by the power Unholy Aura or whose souls are thoroughly corrupt. The abomination that comes has an equal chance (1d6) of being (1–2) a Vindictive Daemon, 3–4) a Knowledgeable Daemon, or (5–6) a Guardian Daemon (for stats, see the ritual Summon Daemon on page 94).
novice: [Act] Test [Res]. Teleport 2 moves. Take 1D4 dmg (ign. Armor). Fail = Daemon enters.
adept: [Act] No dmg. Fail = Can stop Daemon with [Res].
master: [Act] Take passenger (dmg/corr). Fail = Can stop Daemon with [Res].

name: Thorn cloak
description: The plants in nature are usually seen as still and reactive rather than aggressive and active. Experienced green weavers know better and can use surrounding vines, thorns and roots to defend themselves and their allies.
novice: [Act] +1D4 Armor (+1D6 stationary).
adept: [Act] Protect allies +1D4 (melee range).
master: [Act] 1D10 retal dmg (ign. Armor).

name: Tormenting spirits
description: The world is old and many spirits linger from days past; nature spirits in dirt and water, or dead heroes who are yet to pass over to the other side. Some mystics can wake spirits to life and make them attack their enemies. The enemies are beset with these fiery spirits who tear at their clothes, equipment, hair and flesh. At best, the target cannot act; at worst , the target is driven mad or even dies from the attacks.
novice: [Act] Target fails conc. 2nd chance fail tests. Sustained.
adept: [Act] 1D4 [Res] dmg/turn (ign. Armor). 0 [Res] = Death/Insanity.
master: [Act] 1D6 [Res] dmg/turn.

name: Weakening hymn
description: Throughout history, many taunting songs have been written about the faint of heart and in these tunes there are debilitating harmonies to be exploited by mystics who know how. The mystic repeatedly sings this infectious theme while fighting, thereby spreading cowardliness and weakness amongst his or her enemies. The song is interrupted if the mystic uses another mystical power or if concentration is lost by taking damage [Resolute –Damage].
novice: [Free] Test [Per←Res]. Wounded enemies 2nd chance to fail tests.
adept: [Free] All enemies (wounded or not).
master: [Free] Fail deals 1D4 dmg (ign. Armor).

name: Wild hunt
description: Davokar's nature may seem dark and full of conflicts, trapped in an eternal cycle of birth, strife and death. But to mystics who have the capability to see the deeper truth, there is a perfect imbalance to this cycle; a higher form of harmony. This insight can be used by the mystic to acquire the help of seemingly hostile creatures of the Beast category. The summoned beasts may not be of the same type as the enemies; otherwise the type is decided by which types occur naturally in the environment. The character dictates how the beasts act during the scene, after which they turn and leave the area.
novice: [Act] Summon 1 weak beast.
adept: [Act] 1 Ordinary or 1D4 Weak beasts.
master: [Act] 1 Challenging, 1D4 Ordinary, or 1D6 Weak beasts.

name: Lessons Learned
description: Thought and memory are delicate things, given to change and decay without notice and through minimal interaction. Spoken word, even when apparently unrelated and innocuous, allows the mystic to play with perception and recollection. The Lessons are interrupted if the mystic uses another mystical power or if concentration is lost.
novice: [Free] Test [Per←Res]. Target gets 2nd chance to fail tests while hearing mystic.
adept: [Free] Test [Per←Res]. Target forgets specific thing (6 words).
master: [Free] Test [Per←Res]. Target follows imperative (12 words). Overrides better judgment.

name: Uron's Breath
description: The gentle hiss of the Serpent God lulls opposition into a state of ease and restfulness, robbing them of their wariness. At all levels of ability, the mystic must maintain a hissing sound, inhibiting common acts of communication, initiating new mystical powers, or extreme bursts of physical exertion (combat remains manageable, but sprinting, for example, would not). Unless noted otherwise, damage will necessitate a Concentration check (pg 130) or end the effect.
novice: [Free] Chain calm [Res←Res]. Targets -1 to [Acc], [Qui], or [Vig] (mystic chooses).
adept: [Free] Targets -1 to ALL three attributes.
master: [Free] Target struggles to stay awake. Fail = Move/Passive actions only.

name: Aorism
description: Oroke broods in a web at the heart of everything, so they say. Each strand of that web stretches out through the shadows of eternity, connecting and interconnecting into the furthest reaches of the dark. A Mystic with a knowledge of the Aorist can reach out at pluck those strands, repeating, extending or slipping through the moment.
novice: [Act] Test [Res]. Re-roll 1 die/turn. Must accept second result. Lasts 10 turns/scene.
adept: [Act] Target rolls with Favor (NPC) or Disfavor (PC). Sustained.
master: [Act] Vanish. Reappear anywhere reachable (2 moves/turn). Act immediately (highest init).

name: Oroke's Blessing
description: The primal essence of the spider god pervades every culture, civilised or otherwise. The mystic who embraces, rather than fears, the embodiment of the spider can tap into the deep potential of all children of Oroke.
novice: [Act] Target point. Hear/[Vig] tests from that location for Scene.
adept: [Act] Test [Res←Res] to terrify. Target flees/cowers. Test/turn to recover.
master: [Act] Locate specific person/object. Knows path. Target cannot hide.

name: Displacement
description: During the time that the Ordo Septimus has explored, they have mastered the subtle arts of small exchanges of place – nothing like those achieved through Magic Circles or artefacts; these subtle movements serve as a means to confound and confused as much as anything. However, even acts so small punch small holes in the fabric of the world and none are entirely without risk; any roll of 20 when activating this Power pokes dangerous holes in the Walls of Reality (see here).
novice: [Act] Test [Acc←Qui]. Displace object from hand (to mystic or random).
adept: [Act] Test [Res←Res]. Swap location with target (2 moves range). Mystic checks [Res] or Despair.
master: [Act] Test [Acc]. Displace object INSIDE target. 1D6 penetrating dmg/turn on move. Remove with surgery/magic.

name: Bushcraft
description: The character can survive on meager resources and is used to finding food and shelter in harsh terrain...
novice: [Spec] Test [Vig] to find food/water. 1D6 rations (move) or 1D10 (stay). Can take multiple times.

name: Contacts
description: The character has served in an organization or traveled far and wide, and has therefore spun a wide web of contacts...
novice: [Spec] Test [Per] to recall helpful contact.

name: Pariah
description: The character belongs to a race which is ill-reputed among the ruling majority and is more or less openly discriminated against...
novice: [Pas] Social interactions: roll twice, take worst. Own race: 2nd chance to succeed. Start with 5 shillings.

name: Long-lived
description: Once adulthood is reached, the aging process of the character slows down...
novice: [Pas] Slow aging. No mechanical effect.

name: Privileged
description: The character belongs to a race of high social standing within its society...
novice: [Pas] Own society: 2nd chance on social tests. Start with 50 thaler.

name: Short-lived
description: The character's life is short, even under favorable living conditions...
novice: [Pas] Short life. No mechanical effect.

name: Robust
description: The character belongs to a race of creatures that are naturally tall and often continue to grow their entire lives. But there are variations: some grow quickly, others more slowly while some hardly seems to grow at all.
novice: [Spec] Ignore 1D4 dmg/hit. Deal +1D4 melee dmg once/turn. Def based on [Qui-2]. Light armor only (cost x2).
adept: [Spec] Ignore 1D6 dmg/hit. Deal +1D6 melee dmg once/turn. Def based on [Qui-3]. Light armor only (cost x3).
master: [Spec] Ignore 1D8 dmg/hit. Deal +1D8 melee dmg once/turn. Def based on [Qui-4]. Light armor only (cost x4).

name: Shapeshifter
description: The character has the capability to borrow the appearance of others for a period of time. For young changelings this ability comes naturally, and it can be hard for them not to adopt the appearance and mannerisms of people around them. Mature changelings usually develop greater control over the trait.
novice: [Free] Test [Res]. Adopt false shape for Scene. [Dis←Vig] to fool others.
adept: [Free] Test [Res]. Mimic specific person. 50% miss chance vs multiple enemies. Conc [Res] + [Res-Dmg].
master: [Free] Test [Res]. Mimic specific person for Scene. Fooling acquaintances requires 2 tests.

name: Survival instinct
description: The character belongs to a race with a powerful life-force and an equally powerful will to survive. For some individuals this energy shows itself in clamorous hollering and an acute restlessness; for others it manifests itself in a more useful survival instinct.
novice: [Free] Extra Move Action 1/scene.
adept: [Rea] +1D4 Armor.
master: [Free] Sacrifice Move for Extra Combat Action 1/scene.

name: Wisdom of the Ages
description: Through the eons, the elves have amassed a vast collective wisdom; a deep well of knowledge and insights which many elves can access through meditation. The character is one of those who may use the know-how of previous generations to solve problems at hand. It is not without risks; in the twilight of the world, the process spawns corruption. Wisdom of the Ages gives temporary corruption as if it was a mystical power.
novice: [Act] Test [Res]. Access Novice ability (not mystic) for Scene.
adept: [Act] Shorter trance.
master: [Act] Test [Res]. Access Adept ability.

name: Earth Bound
description: The creature is bound to the world in an intimate way, as if originating from the bones of the world and still being part of its foundation. It has no soul and suffers damage instead of corruption; temporary corruption causes bleeding wounds on its body. Permanent corruption instead causes a permanent reduction to the basis for calculating the creatures Pain Threshold. In practice, this means that the Pain Threshold is reduced by 1 for every other point the creature suffers in permanent corruption. Its Toughness is not affected. If the Pain Threshold is reduced to zero, the creature dies of internal bleeding and failing organs. Once dead, the creature cannot become undead and it cannot be contacted with the ritual Necromancy. The corpse decays and reunites with the slop and dust of creation, without leaving any kind of spiritual trace behind.
novice: [Pas] Take Dmg instead of Corr. Perm Corr reduces Pain Threshold. Dies at 0 PT. No undead/necromancy.

name: Acidic attack
description: Either the creature's unarmed attack or its Natural Weapon is covered in acid so that each hit has a corrosive side effect on the target. The acid must first penetrate the target's Armor to deal damage, even if the initial attack does. Removing the acid from either body or armor requires that someone spends an Action and makes a successful Cunning test. Acidic Attack requires the Acidic Blood trait, at the same level or higher.
novice: I [Rea] 3 acid dmg for 3 turns.
adept: II [Rea] 4 acid dmg for 4 turns.
master: III [Rea] 5 acid dmg for 5 turns.

name: Acidic blood
description: The creature's blood is corrosive, and sprays all around when the creature is hit by attacks. Whoever hits the creature in melee combat, and manages to damage it, must make a Defense test or be hit by the acidic blood. Removing the acid from either body or armor requires that someone spends an Action and makes a successful Cunning test (wash it away with water, dirt, sand or something similar).
novice: I [Rea] Melee attacker tests [Def] or 3 acid dmg/3 turns. Remove [Cun].
adept: II [Rea] 4 acid dmg/4 turns.
master: III [Rea] 5 acid dmg/5 turns.

name: Alternative damage
description: The creature's attack harms a specific Attribute instead of Toughness, usually Strong or Resolute. If not specified in the monster description, the Game Master decides which one. This kind of damage affects all rolls made using that Attribute. Alternative Damage heals, and can be healed, just like ordinary damage.
